analysis: Examined base text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md lines 788-1668 (sandbox, setup, installer events, add-on commands, stop/restart/status/doctor). The changes are documentation only. The change map shows a new repeatable `setup --disk <volume>` option (head 1064, 1078) and Work disk check and plan lines (head 1094-1132). It also touches the summary, status and event tables (head 1187, 1213, 1249-1258, 1335). These docs relate to TB-013, A-019 and T-061: the CLI downloads install.sh over TLS only and runs it as the owner. Per the patch excerpt, the CLI makes each disk path absolute, checks it with statfs and passes it to the add-on installer, which needs add-on 1.2.0 or later. Placing VM images and jobs on external volumes is add-on behavior. It is outside the provider prefix-cache CacheVolume controls in T-041. The visible head excerpt is truncated, so the full disk-validation text was not seen, including any /Volumes/<name> mount checks. No head text for the progress/status field changes was supplied. No regression to TB-013 is evident from the visible text: execution is still the owner's, and the script trust model is unchanged. The installer now receives operator-supplied paths as arguments. If the integration pass sees SandboxSetupCommand.swift, it should confirm that --disk values are passed as discrete argv entries, not interpolated into shell text. The threat model's TB-013/T-061 description may need to mention work-disk path forwarding. That is documentation drift, not a vulnerability.
